newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CUTS OIL PRICE BY 1.88 PCT.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CUTS OIL PRICE BY 1.88 PCT.

text.p: Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Friday it was cutting its domestic oil prices by an average 1.88 percent, effective from Saturday, following sound profits in July.
Chinese Petroleum's July earnings were T$2.435 billion, T$551 million above the targetted T$1.884 billion, the company said in a statement.
Officials attributed the sound July profit to falling world crude prices in the period, despite a sharp decline in the Taiwan dollar in July.
The company said its crude oil import prices in July averaged $17.44 a barrel, lower than its budgeted cost of $17.50 and $1.22 lower than its June purchase price.

Chinese Petroleum budgeted its crude imports based on the exchange rate of T$27.50 to the U.S. dollar for July, but the company actually paid an average of T$28.01 for its imports, the statement said.

The company said in a statement that it forecast its oil import costs of $16.44 per barrel in the future based on a forecast exchange rate of T$28.5 to the U.S. dollar. A company spokesman said the forecast extended until the end of the fiscal year in June 1998.
A company official based in Singapore said each T$1.00 drop against the dollar could cost Chinese Petroleum T$6 billion a year.
The company said it would review its oil price and make adjustments each month.
On Friday, the Taiwan dollar ended at T$28.739 to the U.S. dollar against Thursday's T$28.639 finish.

The Taiwan dollar has been tumbling in the past few weeks, touching a nine-year low in late July. Last week it fell 2.8 percent after the central bank allowed the Taiwan dollar to fall below T$28 for the first time since 1989.

Chinese Petroleum raised prices of petroleum products by an average nine percent on January 1 and a further 2.97 percent on April 4 to cover what had been a rapidly growing accumulated budget deficit.
Chinese Petroleum imports some 560,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil and up to 250,000 bpd of products, including liquid natural gas. It exports around 120,000 bpd of diesel and fuel oil.
